title: Which rule decided a web transaction, from the logs
aliases: which rule fired in the logs

rulelabel-block-only.statement: `rulelabel` and `ruletype` are filled only when a Block rule applied; an allowed transaction has neither, so an empty `rulelabel` does not mean no rule matched.

quotes: %s{rulelabel},"The name of the rule that was applied to the transaction. Applies only to Block rules, not Allow."
%s{ruletype},"The type of policy. Applies only to Block rules, not Allow."

separate-layer-labels.statement: URL Filtering and Cloud App Control each have their own rule-name field (`urlfilterrulelabel`, `apprulelabel`), so one record can name both when both layers evaluated, and the allow-side rule is visible there even when `rulelabel` is empty.
separate-layer-labels.conditions: The fields are documented separately; that both can be filled in one record follows from both policies evaluating one transaction.

quotes: %s{urlfilterrulelabel},The name of the rule that was applied to the URL filter
%s{apprulelabel},The name of the rule that was applied to the application

category-source.statement: `urlcat` records the category the transaction was judged under, and `urlcatmethod` records where that categorization came from, which is how logs reveal a URL's actual category membership.

quotes: %s{urlcatmethod},"Refers to the source of the URL's category.
